FS2 · Pattern Hunt

AI Conceptual Understanding

Teaching route

Hook image → retrieval → vocabulary → misconception → teacher think-aloud → guided role task → resource quest → independent judgement → RAG target.

Curriculum intent

Build AI literacy through explicit vocabulary, modelling, guided practice and visible student evidence.

Vocabulary

Input · output · data · model · prompt · evidence · source · bias · privacy · human oversight · safeguard.

Misconception

AI understands like a person.

Support and stretch

Support: sentence stems, vocabulary cards, paired talk, visual prompts. Stretch: compare two outputs, identify trade-offs and defend the stronger decision.

QA evidence

Collect student artefacts showing claim, evidence, limitation, safeguard and RAG next step.

Teacher resources: Pattern Hunt

Hook image → retrieval → vocabulary → misconception → teacher think-aloud → guided role task → resource quest → independent judgement → RAG target.

Curriculum intent

Build AI literacy through explicit vocabulary, modelling, guided practice and visible student evidence.

Vocabulary

Input · output · data · model · prompt · evidence · source · bias · privacy · human oversight · safeguard.

Misconception

AI understands like a person.

Support and stretch

Support: sentence stems, vocabulary cards, paired talk, visual prompts. Stretch: compare two outputs, identify trade-offs and defend the stronger decision.

QA evidence

Collect student artefacts showing claim, evidence, limitation, safeguard and RAG next step.

Topic Search

Foundation Stage · Ages 4-5 · AI Buddy: Dot · Discovery Bot

FS2 AI Literacy

Natural or machine helper. Sensors, sorting and safe adult help.

AI Conceptual Understanding
FS2AI Conceptual Understanding

Pattern Hunt

Explain how the system learns, represents data, makes predictions and produces outputs.

Topic-specific resource links

🔗 Topic lesson deck🔗 BBC Newsround: What is AI?🔗 AI4K12 Five Big Ideas poster🔗 Google Quick Draw🔗 Long-term plan spreadsheet🔗 Whole-school AI roadmap

Immersive activity

Pupils use the visual hook to identify the AI system, the people affected, the evidence required, the benefit, the limitation and the safeguard. They work as designer, user, evidence checker and safety lead.

  • Bronze: identify what the system does.
  • Silver: explain what data, rule, model or prompt may affect the output.
  • Gold: judge one benefit, one risk and one improvement.
  • Platinum: defend a decision using evidence and a safeguard.

Big idea

Explain how the system learns, represents data, makes predictions and produces outputs. In this topic, pupils connect the concept to Pattern Hunt using evidence rather than guesswork.

Teacher model

Think aloud: define the problem, name the data or evidence, test the response, identify one risk, then improve the prompt, rule, design or safeguard.

Common misconception

AI understands like a person.

Lesson sequence

  1. Retrieval: three key words and one likely misconception.
  2. Visual hook: inspect the image and identify input, output, data, people, benefit and risk.
  3. Teacher model: claim → evidence → limitation → safeguard.
  4. Guided pair task: designer, user, evidence checker, safety lead.
  5. Independent judgement: answer, improve, RAG next step.

Assessment evidence

Prompt log, model card, audit note, evidence table, risk card, policy statement, annotated output or design improvement.

Topic resources: Pattern Hunt

  • Bronze: identify what the system does.
  • Silver: explain what data, rule, model or prompt may affect the output.
  • Gold: judge one benefit, one risk and one improvement.
  • Platinum: defend a decision using evidence and a safeguard.

Big idea

Judge privacy, fairness, consent, oversight, accountability and wider impact. In this topic, pupils connect the concept to Private or Safe to Share? using evidence rather than guesswork.

Teacher model

Think aloud: define the problem, name the data or evidence, test the response, identify one risk, then improve the prompt, rule, design or safeguard.

Common misconception

AI safety only means passwords.

Lesson sequence

  1. Retrieval: three key words and one likely misconception.
  2. Visual hook: inspect the image and identify input, output, data, people, benefit and risk.
  3. Teacher model: claim → evidence → limitation → safeguard.
  4. Guided pair task: designer, user, evidence checker, safety lead.
  5. Independent judgement: answer, improve, RAG next step.

Assessment evidence

Prompt log, model card, audit note, evidence table, risk card, policy statement, annotated output or design improvement.

Topic resources: Private or Safe to Share?

AI Conceptual Understanding
Year 8AI Conceptual Understanding

Training vs Deployment

Explain how the system learns, represents data, makes predictions and produces outputs.

Topic-specific resource links

🔗 Topic lesson deck🔗 UAE AI Strategy 2031🔗 UNESCO AI competency framework🔗 Khan Academy Responsible AI Framework🔗 Long-term plan spreadsheet🔗 Whole-school AI roadmap

Immersive activity

Pupils use the visual hook to identify the AI system, the people affected, the evidence required, the benefit, the limitation and the safeguard. They work as designer, user, evidence checker and safety lead.

  • Bronze: identify what the system does.
  • Silver: explain what data, rule, model or prompt may affect the output.
  • Gold: judge one benefit, one risk and one improvement.
  • Platinum: defend a decision using evidence and a safeguard.

Big idea

Explain how the system learns, represents data, makes predictions and produces outputs. In this topic, pupils connect the concept to Training vs Deployment using evidence rather than guesswork.

Teacher model

Think aloud: define the problem, name the data or evidence, test the response, identify one risk, then improve the prompt, rule, design or safeguard.

Common misconception

AI understands like a person.

Lesson sequence

  1. Retrieval: three key words and one likely misconception.
  2. Visual hook: inspect the image and identify input, output, data, people, benefit and risk.
  3. Teacher model: claim → evidence → limitation → safeguard.
  4. Guided pair task: designer, user, evidence checker, safety lead.
  5. Independent judgement: answer, improve, RAG next step.

Assessment evidence

Prompt log, model card, audit note, evidence table, risk card, policy statement, annotated output or design improvement.

Topic resources: Training vs Deployment
